<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **40** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-user-grants-cache.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/lifecycle-verb-rls-operation.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**35** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ae816c40b75f75ccbb8a512c3f17b36608df3ed4`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-user-grants-cache.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/lifecycle-verb-rls-operation.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/permission.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ae816c40b75f75ccbb8a512c3f17b36608df3ed4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `16929c5e79a16cc1bb67a7f371184dd61002ca74` — the merge of head `aa6ae4c43c896a5836223ceb0719b15cbdd517cb` into base `ae816c40b75f75ccbb8a512c3f17b36608df3ed4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 16929c5e79a16cc1bb67a7f371184dd61002ca74 && git checkout 16929c5e79a16cc1bb67a7f371184dd61002ca74
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ae816c40b75f75ccbb8a512c3f17b36608df3ed4 aa6ae4c43c896a5836223ceb0719b15cbdd517cb && git checkout -B drift-repro ae816c40b75f75ccbb8a512c3f17b36608df3ed4 && git merge --no-ff aa6ae4c43c896a5836223ceb0719b15cbdd517cb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ae816c40b75f75ccbb8a512c3f17b36608df3ed4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ae816c40b75f75ccbb8a512c3f17b36608df3ed4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aa6ae4c43c896a5836223ceb0719b15cbdd517cb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/lifecycle-verb-rls-operation.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-rls-filter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/platform-ownership-policies.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-user-grants-cache.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/purge.ts, packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/restore.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/verify/src/handle.ts, packages/spec/liveness/permission.json, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx

Inputs read: card #30237 body and all 32 comments (one page); PR #31438 body and file list (29 files, +775/-229); the net diff `origin/main...aa6ae4c4` (merge base `db502314`); the 42 check-runs on the head. Rulings judged against: hand-over 6690307585, Q5 = A 6676415868, Q3 = A 6676408264, ruling 6691358077 (app-authored bodies never delete for good), the PR 2 review 6689562965 (should-fix 1 is this PR's landing condition), claim 6718158676, amendment 6718183894, spec consent 6718336940. The read-only shape held: nothing built, run or re-run; code outside the diff was read with `git show` / `git grep` at the head.

### ① Derived judgments

**The hits file, against consent 6718336940 and Q5 = A.**

- Right. (a) `ObjectPermissionVerbTarget` (`permission.zod.ts:137-147`) gains exactly `allowRestoreOwnDeleted` and `manageRecycleBin`. Its only consumers outside the evaluator are `api-surface/security.json` (a name list, no row owed) and `ui/packages/permissions/src/MePermissionsProvider.tsx:487`, a `Record<string, ObjectPermissionVerbTarget>` that is not exhaustive; nothing breaks on the widening.
- Right, with one reading to record. (b) `objectPermissionGrants` (`:294-296`) adds `manageRecycleBin: read ∧ (manageRecycleBin ∨ modifyAll)` and `allowRestoreOwnDeleted: read ∧ (allowRestoreOwnDeleted ∨ manageRecycleBin ∨ modifyAll)`. `read` is the fold's existing read cell (`allowRead ∨ viewAllRecords ∨ modifyAllRecords`, `:286`), not the bare `allowRead` the consent spells. That is the same read half every bounded cell uses (edit, delete, export) and the `allowDelete` describe states it; a `viewAllRecords` holder can read the object, so bounding on it is the ruling's "allowRead bounds both" as the file already means it. `allowDelete` appears in neither cell. `OBJECT_PERMISSION_VERBS` and `can()` are untouched (no hunk).
- Right. (c) The `[PLANNED] … Not read yet` describes and the docblock (`:682-695`) now say the keys are read, name the fold and its four sentences, and say where the engine's own-entry half lives.
- Right. The two liveness rows flip `planned` → `live`, dated 2026-11-08, citing `OPERATION_TO_PERMISSION`, `objectPermissionGrants` and `assertCallerMayRestoreEntry`; `state-counts/permission.md` moves 38/2 → 40/0. `Spec property liveness` is green on the head.

**One fold (#18785).** Right. The evaluator asks `objectPermissionGrants(merged, permKey)` (`permission-evaluator.ts:337-338`); `mergeResolvedObjectPermissions` (`:250-268`) merges every `true` boolean key, so the two new keys reach the fold. `MODIFY_ALL_WRITE_KEYS` is derived from the map and set and decides nothing (its docblock says so); `crudBucketForOperation` buckets restore → `update`, purge → `delete` for the ADR-0066 ⑤ AND-gate and the super-user bypass bit, which only narrows. Core's `GRANT_BITS` (`effective-object-permissions.ts:336-339`) lists the keys and every pass that uses it (`foldSuperUserWildcardGrants`, `materializePlainWildcardCoverage`, `grantsAnyVerb`) calls the spec fold. `restore.ts:392-394` asks `objectPermissionGrants(permission, RECYCLE_BIN_GRANT_KEYS.manage)`. No second copy of the implication exists in the diff or the live tree.

**`/me/permissions` and the formula path.** Right. The map the Console and the engine's `can()` read now carries the two keys on wildcard-materialised entries; `toEvalPermissions` (`formula/src/eval-permissions.ts:50-69`) parses each entry with `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema`, which extends the base shape that has held both keys since #30235, so the wider map is accepted, not refused.

**The mapping and the plugin-security sites the hand-over lists.**

- Right. `OPERATION_TO_PERMISSION` gains `restore: RECYCLE_BIN_GRANT_KEYS.restoreOwnDeleted`, `purge: RECYCLE_BIN_GRANT_KEYS.manage` (`permission-evaluator.ts:83-84`); `DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS` keeps all three members as the backstop (`:97`); the gate asks the fold for a mapped verb before the backstop can answer (`:324-338`).
- Right. Every write-class site now reads `rlsOperationForVerb`: `rls-compiler.ts:1343` (`mapOperationToRLS`, whose default sent a lifecycle verb to `select`), `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts:174-175` and `:374`, `security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts:114` and `:133`, `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts:473`, `platform-ownership-policies.ts:359-361`. The authz epoch bump lists `purge` and `restore` (`:404-405`). Steps 2.6, 2.7 and 2.8 already listed both verbs (`:975`, `:994`, `:1069`, `:1280`).
- Right, by absence of a caller. `security-plugin-authored-row-write.ts:108` still accepts `update | delete` only; its two callers hand it a literal `'update'` (`cbp-write-gate.ts:1121`) or plugin-sharing's own `update | delete` verb (`sharing-service.ts:1344`), so no lifecycle verb reaches it. No change was owed.
- Inert, left as is. `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:2318` (the bulk-write guard target) still keys on `update`/`delete`; it sits inside `if (opCtx.ast)` and the #7809 pin keeps every `purge`/`restore` dispatch AST-free, so it cannot be reached with either verb. See ④ nit.
- Right. `packages/verify/src/handle.ts:605-612` records `purge` and `restore`; `ObservedWrite.operation` widens accordingly and `@objectstack/verify` is in the changeset.
- Right. `resolve-user-grants-cache.ts` keeps `WRITE_OPERATIONS` at insert/update/delete with the reason: the bin never takes a platform object (`recycleBinTakesObject`, Q7) and every watched grant object is `sys_`, so a `purge`/`restore` never touches one. The hand-over offered either answer.

**Security, tried along the brief's lines.**

- Cross-tenant or another person's entry without `manageRecycleBin`: not reachable. `restore` refuses a wall-denied caller before any read (`restore.ts:375`), reads the entry scoped by the engine's own verdict (`:376-380`, `null` for another organization's id), dispatches `restore` on the master's object (object gate: `allowRestoreOwnDeleted`, read-bounded), then in the executor re-checks the recorded verdict (`:388`) and asks `assertCallerMayRestoreEntry` (`:389`): the system passes; `deleted_by === context.userId` passes; otherwise the registered resolver's map must fold to `manageRecycleBin` on the entry's object, and no resolver, a throwing resolver, or a map without the object all refuse `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (`:369-396`). `attributedUserId` is not consulted; capture writes `deleted_by` from `userId`, else `attributedUserId` (`capture.ts:287-293`), so a human credited for a system-authorized delete still matches on their own `userId`. The own-entry check runs after the object gate, so a caller without the key never learns whether an entry exists.
- `purge(entryId)` / `empty(object)`: wall-denied callers answer `false` / `0` before any read (`purge.ts:210`, `:258`); the entry is read under the engine's verdict (`:211-218`); the dispatch on the entry's business object asks `manageRecycleBin`; the executor re-checks the recorded verdict and passes `{ recordedVerdict }` to the bin's driver (`:221-226`, `:260-265`). The permanent delete keeps `where.id` and meets step 2.7 as a delete (floor plus the delete-class sharing verdict in `resolvePreImageFloorDrop`) and the 2.8 master gate.
- `allowDelete` implying restore: nowhere. The two cells omit it; the evaluator tests and the spec test pin `{allowRead, allowDelete}` → `false` for both keys; `security-plugin.test.ts` pins the object gate refusing `{allowRead, allowEdit, allowDelete, viewAllRecords}` for both verbs.
- System context: unchanged. The authz bypass at `:418` is untouched; `recycleBinWallDenies` and `assertCallerMayRestoreEntry` both return early for `isSystem`; the two reads are registered in the system-context census (rows 29d/29e). Ruling 6691358077 holds: `HookDeleteOptions` still omits `permanent`, the hook face (`hook-api.ts:279`) exposes `delete` only, and the sandbox body runner exposes no `restore`, `purge` or `empty`, so an app-authored body still cannot reach the purge verb.
- Deny-first ordering on the purge entry read: sound. The pre-read check and the read use the same engine verdict (`recycleBinWallDenies` and `driverReadScope` both fall back to `engineLayer0Verdict`), so a `deny` can never reach the driver as "no scope"; the executor's second check uses the recorded verdict when one exists, exactly as `driverReadScope` does. Under `single` the verdict is `none` for everyone, which is the posture, not a hole.

**Landing condition (PR 2 review should-fix 1).** Closed as asked. The two object-level dispatches carry `recordedVerdict: opCtx.tenantLayer0Verdict` (`purge.ts:221-226`, `:260-265`), and a `deny` verdict, engine or recorded, refuses before the driver is reached. The pre-dispatch entry read cannot carry a recorded verdict (nothing has been recorded yet); it is scoped by the engine's verdict and preceded by the deny check, which is the fall-open the review named. Note that plugin-security records `opCtx.tenantLayer0Verdict` only inside `if (opCtx.ast)` (`authz-middleware.ts:2414`), so for these AST-less dispatches the recorded path is exercised only by a custom middleware today; the engine's own verdict decides.

**Check-runs on the head** (read 2026-11-08 08:00Z): 42 check-runs; 13 success (Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, filter), 7 skipped, 22 in progress (Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, two scoped Lints, Live E2E UI, Test Core 1-8, Type Check × 4). Every in-progress family is NOT MEASURED by this record, `check:generated`, `check:system-context-census` and the typecheck of the widened `ObjectPermissionVerbTarget` among them. None red.

### ② Semver level

Confirmed. `.changeset/30237-recycle-bin-permission-reader.md` declares `patch` for `@objectstack/spec`, `plugin-security`, `core`, `objectql` and `verify`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial, matching the PR body and the claim. The authorable surface is unchanged: both keys have been authorable since #30235, no key, value or default moves, so `none` is right and takes `patch` (AGENTS.md step 3). The widening is real and named: a granted key (or `modifyAllRecords`) now opens `restore` / `purge`, which every non-system caller was refused; `ObjectPermissionVerbTarget` and `ObservedWrite.operation` widen; `objectPermissionGrants` answers two targets it did not. No narrowing hides in it: a caller holding neither key is refused exactly as before, `allowDelete` grants nothing new, and the wall-deny answers (`null` / `false` / `0`) replace a path the backstop refused anyway. `Check Changeset` is green. The changeset body carries no `Skills-docs:` line (see ③).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, attribution `os-project-manager`; no outside login to name.
- Dev deviations (report 6719012131), each judged: (1) surface beyond the claim, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` rows 29d/29e plus the regenerated register, generated `content/docs/references/**`, `liveness/state-counts`, `spec/permission.test.ts`: all forced by `check:system-context-census` / `check:generated` or asked by the seat; right, and the seat should name them in the amendment since 6718183894 names `engine.ts` and the spec hunk only. (2) The purge pre-read cannot carry the recorded verdict: right, see ①. (3) `restore` gets the same deny refusal as purge/empty: right, the same fall-open class, and row 29d says so. (4) `WRITE_OPERATIONS` kept: right, the hand-over offered it. (5) Merge commit with git's default message: no rule touched.
- Dev acceptance notes, each confirmed in the tree: the recorded verdict is written only on AST operations (`authz-middleware.ts:2414`); the CBP master gate and delegated-admin gate judge no id-less `restore`/`purge` (2.8 runs for them and finds no master to judge; a by-id `purge` is judged); a super-user wildcard's map now shows both bin keys on `sys_` objects where the engine refuses `400` (a report of the grant, harmless, no change asked); the stale `[REMOVED]` describes are graded in ④.
- `security_findings: "withheld"` in the dev report, where every earlier report on this card wrote `"none"`. The seat should read what was withheld before ACCEPT; this record found no security defect of its own.
- `Skills-docs:` line: hand-over 6690307585 says every PR of this card cites #30847 on a `Skills-docs:` line, and PR 3's body does (`Skills-docs: follow-up #30847`); this PR's body and changeset carry none. No gate enforces it. A prose-face nit for the PR body.
- Carried for the seat, outside this diff and not graded against it: plugin-sharing's own by-id write middleware (`sharing-plugin.ts:1510`) branches on `update`/`delete` only, so a by-id permanent delete (`purge`) is not asked its `canDelete`. plugin-security's step 2.7 judges that write as a delete and its floor drop asks the same delete-class sharing verdict (`resolvePreImageFloorDrop`, `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts:275-293`), so wherever the platform ownership floor applies the refusal is preserved; where no floor policy applies, plugin-sharing's gate was the only per-record write authority and the by-id `purge` passes it unasked. PR 2 shipped the dispatch and this PR makes it grantable; a follow-up card or a one-line pin in plugin-sharing is owed, not a change to this PR's surface.
- Hand-written docs outside the diff that this PR makes false: `content/docs/permissions/permissions-matrix.mdx:78` and `content/docs/protocol/objectql/security.mdx:111` still say the `restore`/`purge` operations do not exist and are denied unconditionally. Docs prose, not spec; a follow-up, named here so it is not lost.
- `open_questions`: none in the report. `pr5_spec_need`: unmeasured by the dev, reported before PR 5 starts.
- The spec hunk is inside consent 6718336940 (a, b, c and the two liveness rows). The fix ④ asks for (the retirement prose in the same file) is prose outside that consent's list; the seat records the maintainer's word, or its own reading that a prescription string is a prose face, before the delta.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`, against Q5 = A, consent 6718336940, and its first consumer (the evaluator's object gate).

- The two cells implement the ruling as written; the evaluator reads them through the merged entry so the read half may come from a different set than the grant, as for edit and delete; core's map, the Console's fold and the engine's own-entry check all read the one function. The widened `ObjectPermissionVerbTarget` docblock says the keys are read for `restore` / `purge` and that no verb resolves to them, which the unchanged `OBJECT_PERMISSION_VERBS` makes true.
- **Should-fix (prose made false by this PR).** The same file still publishes, at `:527-542` (the `restore` / `purge` guidance strings), `:620-640` (the tombstone docblock) and `:654-670` (the `allowRestore` / `allowPurge` `retiredKey` prescriptions), that "the `restore` ObjectQL operation it claimed to gate has never shipped (roadmap M2)", that "a dispatched `restore` / `purge` stays denied fail-closed by the permission evaluator's destructive-operation backstop", and that "the bit returns with the M2 lifecycle initiative". On this head the operations ship, the object gate answers them from `allowRestoreOwnDeleted` / `manageRecycleBin`, the backstop decides nothing (the evaluator's own docblock now says so), and the bits were respelled on purpose and never return. This is the parse-time prescription an author sees and it is regenerated verbatim into `content/docs/references/api/auth.mdx`, `api/protocol.mdx` and `security/permission.mdx` in this very diff, so the PR publishes a false security statement ("stays denied") beside the true one. The card already carried the obligation: #30577's review should-fix 2 (6665087359) says the reader PR re-points "the `restore` / `purge` guidance, the `allowRestore` / `allowPurge` tombstone text and the `liveness/permission.json` notes at D5's answer (respelled; the tombstones stay through the ADR-0087 kit schedule)". The two dead liveness rows (`permission.json:94`, `:100`, "stays denied fail-closed via DESTRUCTIVE_OPERATIONS … the key RETURNS with M2") are the same stroke. The tombstones themselves stay; only the sentences change, to: the key was retired, the recycle bin (ADR-0148) ships `restore` / `purge` under the new spellings `allowRestoreOwnDeleted` / `manageRecycleBin`, delete this key and grant those. No effect on enforcement, so not a must-fix; a contract-prose defect, so not a nit. The protocol-18 conversion, retired-key and registry-template texts describe the protocol-18 state and are left alone.

Implementing files in the diff, each against the contract it implements.

- `permission-evaluator.ts`: agrees sentence by sentence with Q5 = A and #18785 (one fold, backstop stays, Modify-All class derived). `crudBucketForOperation` folds restore → `update`, purge → `delete`, the same classes `lifecycle-verb-rls-operation.ts` declares. Holds.
- `lifecycle-verb-rls-operation.ts`: the docblock now lists every reader of the mapping; the map itself (`transfer/restore → update`, `purge → delete`) is unchanged. Holds.
- `rls-compiler.ts`, `security-plugin-rls-filter.ts`, `security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts`, `security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts`, `platform-ownership-policies.ts`: each reads `rlsOperationForVerb` once and keys on the result; a by-id `purge` resolves its row through `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch` as a delete, and the id-less dispatches resolve no row, as the comments say. Hold.
- `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`: the epoch bump covers the write set; the step-3 comment is now true (composition maps the verb itself). **Nit:** `:2318` still keys the bulk-write guard target on `update`/`delete` while the hand-over asked each such site to read the mapping or list `purge`; it is unreachable with a lifecycle verb (AST-only, #7809 pin), so an accepted deviation or a one-line follow-up, not a change on this head.
- `explain-engine.ts`: **Should-fix.** The file's own contract (`:1206-1214`, rewritten in this diff) is that the record story "stays the door's on the day they can be granted", and this PR is that day. Two sites still key on the raw `engineOp` where the door keys on the mapped class: `:2017` picks the sharing write gate as `engineOp === 'delete' ? canDeleteRecord : canEditRecord`, so a by-id `purge` is explained against `canEdit`, while the door (step 2.7's `resolvePreImageFloorDrop`, asked with `rlsOperationForVerb('purge') === 'delete'`) asks the delete-class verdict; and `:2033-2036` says "restore and purge have no by-id door (the object gate refuses both), so nothing defers them", which is false now that the by-id purge has a door. `ExplainOperation` includes `purge` (`EXPLAIN_TO_ENGINE_OP:252`), so `security/explain` can report an edit-share-admitted row as writable for a purge the door refuses (ADR-0111 D3). The fix is `rlsOperationForVerb(engineOp)` at `:2017` (the file already imports it for `:1847` and `:3390`) and the comment at `:2033-2036`; `:1979` and `:2139` want the same reading for the message to name the right gate. A report defect, not an enforcement one.
- `effective-object-permissions.ts` (core): `GRANT_BITS` carries the keys; the super-user fold and plain-wildcard coverage pull them `true` through the spec fold, so the map reports what the server grants (Q5 = A: `modifyAllRecords` implies both). Holds.
- `resolve-user-grants-cache.ts`: comment only; the reason given is true in the tree (`recycleBinTakesObject` excludes `sys_`/`cloud_`/`ai_`). Holds.
